content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; true prices often dip below forecast before rebounding.
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is positive, especially in early days of the forecast window.
- When sentiment history includes multiple consecutive positive values, model overreacts and forecasts higher than true outcome.
- Model underestimates price peaks in the middle of the forecast horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — true prices often revert to prior 10-15 day averages after sharp spikes.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the first 5-7 days of the 30d horizon, especially when sentiment is volatile or recently positive.
